title: O God, My Strength, My Hope
description: O God, My Strength, My Hope in Tonic Solfa to BOYLSTON, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 425 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Prayer for Self-Consecration”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to BOYLSTON; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O God, my strength, my hope, On thee I cast my care, With hum-ble con-fi-dence look up, And know thou hear-est prayer.

lines: O God, my strength, my hope,
On thee I cast my care,
That looks to thee when sin is near,
Till thou my patient spirit guide

licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to BOYLSTON by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
